angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 243,495 km at 6.26 pc = 0.52 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 159.6634 +/- 0.0341 mas (same row, RUWE 1.32): 6.26 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.35 solar radii from Morin et al., arXiv:0808.1423, Table 1: radius 0.35 solar radii (theoretical radius; R sin i = 0.37(2)) (https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1423): 243,495 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.39 solar masses from Morin et al., arXiv:0808.1423, Table 1: mass 0.39 solar masses (https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1423); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3345 K from TESS Input Catalog 8.2 (VizieR IV/39/tic82), TIC 247985094: Teff (https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/VizieR?-source=IV/39/tic82). Spin inclination 60 degrees and rotation period 1.06 d from Morin et al., arXiv:0808.1423, Table 1: rotation period 1.06 d and an axis 60 degrees from the line of sight, the values its magnetic maps were made with (https://arxiv.org/abs/0808.1423). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: TESS Input Catalog 8.2 (VizieR IV/39/tic82), TIC 247985094: Teff (https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/VizieR?-source=IV/39/tic82)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/eq-pegasi-a.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.941, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 896 A (pscomppars): spectral type M3.5 V, from Curiel et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164...93C/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 896 A (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.75523, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/MNRAS/390/567/table1 (Magnetic field and velocity of mid M dwarfs), column Prot: 1.061 d, the row 0.1 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 5 catalogued periods, 5 of them within 20% of it
